evals.prompt: Review evals/fixtures/diagrams/order-flow.mmd — is this diagram good?
evals.expected_output: A findings report in the exact skill format (12-row verdict table, top 3 fixes as actions) followed by a redraw delivered in the response as Mermaid, including legend and element table. The input fixture stays untouched.
expectations: The report contains a findings table with exactly 12 rule rows
Every verdict is one of: pass, partial, fail, not-applicable (rendered as the four emoji from the skill)
The report starts with a purpose assessment line (rule 1)
Each top fix is phrased as an action, not a restatement of a finding
Rule 2 (legend) is marked as a fail — the fixture has no legend
Rule 4 (names defined) is marked fail or partial — the fixture uses cryptic names like 'Mgr' and 'GW'
Rule 7 (~12 elements) is marked pass or not-applicable — the fixture has 9 elements
A redraw is produced as a Mermaid code block
The redraw includes an element table
The redraw stays within the rulebook element budget (~12 structural elements, up to ~20 steps for flows), excluding the legend
The input fixture file evals/fixtures/diagrams/order-flow.mmd is not modified

evals.prompt: Review all diagrams in evals/fixtures/diagrams/ and rank them by quality.
evals.expected_output: Both diagrams reviewed against the 12 rules and an explicit ranking reported. Fanning out diagram-reviewer agents is acceptable but not required for two small text sources; inline reviews are fine.
expectations: Both diagrams (order-flow and user-signup) are reviewed — each gets per-rule findings (full table or compact per-diagram summary)
An explicit ranking or comparative verdict of the two diagrams is reported
Findings for user-signup.mmd flag the unexplained styling (two nodes carry raw hex fill colors with no legend) under rule 2 or rule 8
Findings reference actual fixture content (node names such as 'Mgr', 'GW', 'SvcA', 'BFF'), not invented elements
